concrete.note: M-grade number = cube strength (MPa), matches ICE's second number in its x/y (cylinder/cube) class labels. Source: Concrete sheet, 'By Strength Class' section. Used as FALLBACK ONLY when cement_type is unknown but M-grade is known -- ifc_india.concrete is now the primary source. See ice_factors.py for selection logic.

rebar.source: Steel, Rebar -- worldsteel 2023 study, world average, cradle-to-gate (Module A1-3). Kept as FALLBACK -- ifc_india.steel_rebar is now the primary source (real Indian production data), see ice_factors.py.

ifc_india.source: IFC India Construction Materials Database -- Methodology Report (IFC/World Bank Group, Nov 2017, built by thinkstep/Sphera using GaBi). Cradle-to-gate (EN 15804 Modules A1-A3), GWP per IPCC AR5.
ifc_india.note: PRIMARY source for concrete and steel rebar factors as of this update -- real India-modeled production data, not adjusted-from-elsewhere. Concrete is given per cement type (OPC/PSC/PPC), NOT per M-grade -- this is a real precision tradeoff vs. ICE's grade-based table, not a strict improvement. Grid-mix assumption embedded in this data is ~2012 (57% hard coal, GaBi 2016 dataset) -- see cea.baseline_grid_factor for the adjustment this implies.

concrete.unit: kgCO2e per kg of ready-mix concrete

OPC.display_name: Ready mix concrete with ordinary Portland cement (OPC)

PSC.display_name: Ready mix concrete with Portland slag cement (25% GGBS)

PPC.display_name: Ready mix concrete with fly-ash cement (30% pozzolana)

cea.source: Central Electricity Authority (CEA) CO2 Baseline Database, v21.0, Nov 2025
cea.baseline_grid_factor_note: IFC's embedded grid-mix assumption is dated to ~2012 generation data (GaBi 2016 dataset). CEA's published series does not extend back to 2012 -- FY2013-14 (0.774 tCO2/MWh) is the NEAREST available published figure, used as an approximation, not an exact 2012 value. This is a documented estimate, not a precise historical match.
cea.note: Only applied to ifc_india-sourced factors' energy-derived fraction (see cea_adjustment.py). NOT applied to the ICE fallback table, since the UK/EU grid baseline ICE assumed has not been extracted from ICE's own methodology documentation -- applying an adjustment without that denominator would mean fabricating a number, so ICE fallback factors are left unadjusted and this gap is stated plainly rather than guessed at.
